newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Member states remain opposed to farm aid cuts.
newsitem.headline: Member states remain opposed to farm aid cuts.

text.p: European Union countries remain strongly hostile to Commission proposals to make cuts in farm aids as part of the 1997/98 farm prices package, an EU member state official said on Wednesday.
"There can be no decision at next week's farm council but the Commission will make a report to ministers," the official said after a discussion by the EU's Special Committee on Agriculture.
Opposition to the proposals to cut sugar storage aids, monthly cereals increments and arable area compensatory aids are opposed by most member states.
"The need for cuts is not accepted and most states expressed the view that agricultural spending should be taken right up the the annual limit," the official added.
The member states were divided over a Commission report on the reform of the fraud-ridden olive oil sector.
Producer countries want to maintain the existing subsidy system and oppose the Commission's preference to link payments to the number of trees.
Spanish-led producers are planning a mass protest at the Farm Council on Monday.
Most consumer countries are reluctant to go against the producers' wishes except for Britain and Sweden which back the tree-based option.
The lack of progress in the Special Agriculture Committee means that the Farm Council on Monday and Tuesday will have no items due for a decision, officials said.
However, the Commission is due to make a progress report on the current negotiations with the United States on meat imports.
A Commission official on Wednesday described the negotiations as "ninety percent agreed".

On Tuesday the U.S. postponed retaliatory action under new legislation which came into force on that day until April 30 in order to allow further negotiations on hygiene standards for poultry meat production.
